slot.subtopic: Magnetic field due to finite wire / polygon loop
slot.brief: Superposition of magnetic fields at the centre of a regular polygon (or a combination of two finite wires/loops); no figure, ask the net B and its direction.

stem: Two concentric coplanar loops are a regular triangle and a regular hexagon. Their apothems are $0.30\ \text{m}$ and $0.20\ \text{m}$, respectively, and each carries $4\ \text{A}$. Viewed from above, their currents are clockwise and anticlockwise, respectively. Find the net field at the centre. Take $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \text{T m A}^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: For a regular n-sided loop with apothem a, the centre field is B = μ₀In sin(π/n)/(2πa). The triangle gives 4√3 μT into the plane; the hexagon gives 12 μT out of the plane. The net field is (12 − 4√3) μT out of the plane.

working:
$B_n=\dfrac{\mu_0 nI}{2\pi a}\sin\dfrac{\pi}{n}$; $B_3=4\sqrt{3}\ \mu\text{T}$ into the plane; $B_6=12\ \mu\text{T}$ out of the plane; $B_{\text{net}}=(12-4\sqrt{3})\ \mu\text{T}$ out of the plane.

Independent check: For a regular n-sided loop with apothem a, the centre field is B = μ₀In sin(π/n)/(2πa). The triangle gives 4√3 μT into the plane; the hexagon gives 12 μT out of the plane. The net field is (12 − 4√3) μT out of the plane.
solution:
For a regular $n$-sided loop of apothem $a$, $B_n=\dfrac{\mu_0 nI}{2\pi a}\sin\dfrac{\pi}{n}$.
The triangle produces $4\sqrt{3}\,\mu\text{T}$ into the plane, while the hexagon produces $12\,\mu\text{T}$ out of the plane.
Thus, $B_{\text{net}}=(12-4\sqrt{3})\,\mu\text{T}$, out of the plane.
